literature.headline_zh: 马尔堡病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期马尔堡病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 该暴发谱系被归类为属于MARV.A.1簇,七例基因组之间具有高度的核苷酸同源性,表明在一次人兽共患病事件后发生了人传人传播。 [10.1038/s41564-026-02540-y]
在假设的基础参数条件下,模型模拟显示,在50天期间,环境对人类的暴露至少占人类感染力的99.3%。 [10.9734/air/2026/v27i61764]
蝙蝠细胞上调 抗病毒药物 效应因子,同时限制炎症放大因子,这一模式通过独立的体内 MARV 感染数据集得到支持。相反,人类细胞在 MARV 感染下激活 抗病毒药物 程序和免疫超激活。 [10.1016/j.celrep.2026.118217]
该研究确定了疫苗干扰的三个核心机制:表位竞争、资源竞争和免疫极化。它强调需要进行体外测试来确认抗原表达水平,以及使用标准化测定来评估 免疫应答 的重要性。 [PMCID:PMC13720360]
研究发现,翼手目 IFN-β 诱导的 IFN 刺激基因库与牙买加果蝠细胞中的同种 IFN-β 相当,表明其在不同蝙蝠家族中的功能功效。 [10.64898/2026.10.24.761547]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The outbreak lineage was classified as belonging to the MARV.A.1 clade, with a high nucleotide identity across the seven genomes, indicating human-to-human transmission following a zoonotic spillover event. [10.1038/s41564-026-02540-y]

Under the assumed baseline parameters, model simulations indicate that environment-to-human exposure accounts for at least 99.3% of the human force of infection over the 50-day period. [10.9734/air/2026/v27i61764]

Bat cells upregulate antiviral effectors while limiting inflammatory amplifiers, a pattern supported by independent in vivo MARV infection datasets. In contrast, human cells activate antiviral programs and immune hyperactivation in response to MARV. [10.1016/j.celrep.2026.118217]

The study identified three core mechanisms of vaccine interference: epitope competition, resource competition, and immune polarization. It emphasized the need for in vitro testing to confirm antigen expression levels and the importance of using standardized assays for evaluating immune responses. [PMCID:PMC13720360]
Among 611 adults who participated in the study, 74.8% (95% CI 71.2%, 78.1%) had good knowledge, and 62.7% (95% CI 58.8%, 66.4%) had positive perception, respectively. [10.1038/s41598-026-76470-4]

news.headline_zh: 马尔堡病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期马尔堡病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 埃塞俄比亚于 2025 年 11 月报告了第一个 暴发 的 马尔堡病毒病,对七个早期病例样本的基因组分析揭示了 暴发 谱系属于 MARV.A.1 分支。暴发 已通过埃塞俄比亚公共卫生研究所 (EPHI) 的逆转录 PCR (RT-PCR) 得到证实。 [news-48d3ce396d4cb5c7]
马尔堡病毒 暴发 已在非洲各地报告,埃塞俄比亚于 2025 年 11 月 14 日确认了其首个 马尔堡病毒。文章指出,尚无针对该疾病的许可 疫苗 或药物,该审查强调了了解该疾病的 流行病学 和 治疗 选项所面临的挑战。 [news-87b516456c3c8ece]
所提供的证据没有用经过验证的英语清楚地报告中心事件。 [news-fe188cc84c0a85e8]
IAVI 已获得 BARDA 授予的 马尔堡病毒 疫苗 候选产品转移制造权。 [news-2e5c97d5bb277a1b]
对来自埃塞俄比亚第一个 暴发 的七个接近完整的 马尔堡病毒 基因组 进行的基因组分析揭示了后 跨物种溢出 人与人之间的 传播。该研究由埃塞俄比亚公共卫生研究所 (EPHI)、联邦卫生部和国际合作者的研究人员进行。 [news-c9e9b5bef46ace22]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Marburg virus news developments.
key_findings_en: Ethiopia reported its first outbreak of Marburg virus disease in November 2025, with genomic analysis of seven early case samples revealing the outbreak lineage belonged to the MARV.A.1 clade. The outbreak was confirmed through reverse transcription PCR (RT–PCR) at the Ethiopian Public Health Institute (EPHI). [news-48d3ce396d4cb5c7]

Marburg virus outbreaks have been reported across Africa, with Ethiopia confirming its first-ever outbreak on 14 November 2025. The article states that no licensed vaccine or drug exists for the disease, and the review highlights the challenges in understanding the disease's epidemiology and treatment options. [news-87b516456c3c8ece]

papers.title: Genomic analysis of early case samples from the 2025 Marburg virus outbreak in Ethiopia.
papers.abstract: In November 2025, Ethiopia reported its first outbreak of Marburg virus disease, with a case fatality rate of 64%. Here we report the analysis of seven near-complete Marburg virus genomes from seven early cases. The outbreak lineage belonged to the MARV.A.1 clade, which is closely related to genomes from historical human cases and bats. A high nucleotide identity across the seven genomes suggests human-to-human transmission after a zoonotic spillover event. These findings highlight the importance of genomic surveillance for outbreak detection, response and preparedness. Phylogenetic analysis of seven Marburg virus genomes from the 2025 outbreak in Ethiopia suggests human-to-human transmission after a spillover event.

papers.title: Species-specific gene programs define divergent antiviral responses in Marburg virus reservoir bats and humans.
papers.abstract: Bats tolerate viruses that cause severe disease in humans. Egyptian rousette bats, the natural reservoirs of Marburg virus (MARV), sustain asymptomatic infection, whereas humans develop severe and fatal disease. To define the basis of this divergence, we establish a comparative framework using primary and immortalized Egyptian rousette and human cells exposed to double-stranded RNA and interferon (IFN). Bat cells upregulate antiviral effectors while limiting inflammatory amplifiers, a pattern further supported by analysis of independent in vivo MARV infection datasets. In contrast, human cells activate antiviral programs and immune hyperactivation in response to MARV. Integrating transcriptomic and proteomic analyses, we identify species-specific immune programs encompassing differential IFN-stimulated gene regulation, apoptotic control, and cytokine signaling. Our findings establish an integrative framework for understanding species-specific antiviral responses associated with MARV reservoir biology, identify pathways linked to immunopathogenesis in humans, and provide a foundation for future studies of host responses to filovirus infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the basis of divergent antiviral responses between Marburg virus reservoir bats and humans, as bats tolerate viruses that cause severe disease in humans.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a comparative framework involving primary and immortalized Egyptian rousette and human cells exposed to double-stranded RNA and interferon (IFN), with analysis based on independent in vivo MARV infection datasets.
analysis.methods: The researchers integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses to identify species-specific immune programs, focusing on differential IFN-stimulated gene regulation, apoptotic control, and cytokine signaling.
analysis.main_results: Bat cells upregulate antiviral effectors while limiting inflammatory amplifiers, a pattern supported by independent in vivo MARV infection datasets. In contrast, human cells activate antiviral programs and immune hyperactivation in response to MARV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal species-specific immune programs that define divergent antiviral responses, offering insights into the mechanisms of MARV reservoir biology and immunopathogenesis in humans.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for understanding host responses to filovirus infection, which could inform surveillance, diagnosis, and future therapeutic strategies for Marburg virus disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on cell culture models and in vivo datasets, but the integration of transcriptomic and proteomic analyses supports a moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the divergent antiviral responses between Marburg virus reservoir bats and humans, highlighting how bat cells upregulate antiviral effectors while limiting inflammatory amplifiers, in contrast to human cells that activate antiviral programs and immune hyperactivation. By integrating transcriptomic and proteomic analyses, the researchers identify species-specific immune programs, including differential IFN-stimulated gene regulation, apoptotic control, and cytokine signaling. These findings offer insights into the mechanisms underlying MARV reservoir biology and immunopathogenesis in humans, potentially informing future studies on host responses to filovirus infection. The study's reliance on cell culture models and in vivo datasets limits the confidence in its conclusions, though the comprehensive approach provides a moderate level of evidence for the observed differences in antiviral responses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解 马尔堡病毒 储存宿主 蝙蝠和人类之间不同 抗病毒药物 反应的基础,因为蝙蝠能够容忍在人类中会引起严重疾病的病毒。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用了一个比较框架,涉及暴露于双链 RNA 和干扰素(IFN)的初级和永生化的埃及 rousette 和人类细胞,并基于独立的体内 MARV 感染数据集进行分析。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员整合了转录组和蛋白质组分析,以识别物种特异性的免疫程序,重点关注差异的 IFN 诱导基因调控、凋亡控制和细胞因子信号传导。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the basis of divergent antiviral responses between Marburg virus reservoir bats and humans, as bats tolerate viruses that cause severe disease in humans.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study used a comparative framework involving primary and immortalized Egyptian rousette and human cells exposed to double-stranded RNA and interferon (IFN), with analysis based on independent in vivo MARV infection datasets.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses to identify species-specific immune programs, focusing on differential IFN-stimulated gene regulation, apoptotic control, and cytokine signaling.
analysis_en.main_results: Bat cells upregulate antiviral effectors while limiting inflammatory amplifiers, a pattern supported by independent in vivo MARV infection datasets. In contrast, human cells activate antiviral programs and immune hyperactivation in response to MARV.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal species-specific immune programs that define divergent antiviral responses, offering insights into the mechanisms of MARV reservoir biology and immunopathogenesis in humans.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for understanding host responses to filovirus infection, which could inform surveillance, diagnosis, and future therapeutic strategies for Marburg virus disease.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on cell culture models and in vivo datasets, but the integration of transcriptomic and proteomic analyses supports a moderate confidence in the findings.

papers.title_zh: 物种特异性基因程序定义了抗病毒药物在储存宿主蝙蝠和人类中的不同反应。
papers.source_body_en: Bats tolerate viruses that cause severe disease in humans. Egyptian rousette bats, the natural reservoirs of Marburg virus (MARV), sustain asymptomatic infection, whereas humans develop severe and fatal disease. To define the basis of this divergence, we establish a comparative framework using primary and immortalized Egyptian rousette and human cells exposed to double-stranded RNA and interferon (IFN). Bat cells upregulate antiviral effectors while limiting inflammatory amplifiers, a pattern further supported by analysis of independent in vivo MARV infection datasets. In contrast, human cells activate antiviral programs and immune hyperactivation in response to MARV. Integrating transcriptomic and proteomic analyses, we identify species-specific immune programs encompassing differential IFN-stimulated gene regulation, apoptotic control, and cytokine signaling. Our findings establish an integrative framework for understanding species-specific antiviral responses associated with MARV reservoir biology, identify pathways linked to immunopathogenesis in humans, and provide a foundation for future studies of host responses to filovirus infection.
papers.abstract_zh: 蝙蝠能够容忍在人类中会引起严重疾病的病毒。埃及 rousette 蝙蝠是马尔堡病毒(MARV)的自然宿主,能够无症状感染,而人类则会发展为严重且致命的疾病。为了定义这种差异的基础,我们建立了一个比较框架,使用暴露于双链 RNA 和干扰素(IFN)的初级和永生化的埃及 rousette 和人类细胞。蝙蝠细胞上调 抗病毒药物 效应因子,同时限制炎症放大因子,这一模式进一步通过独立的体内 MARV 感染数据集分析得到支持。相反,人类细胞在 MARV 感染下激活 抗病毒药物 程序和免疫超激活。通过整合转录组和蛋白质组分析,我们鉴定了物种特异性的免疫程序,包括差异的 IFN 诱导基因调控、凋亡控制和细胞因子信号传导。我们的研究结果建立了一个整合框架,用于理解与 MARV 生物学相关的物种特异性 抗病毒药物 反应,识别了与人类免疫病理学相关的通路,并为未来研究 宿主 对 丝状病毒 感染的反应提供了基础。

papers.title: Quantifying the extinction probability of Marburg virus disease outbreaks: A continuous-time Markov chain model integrating a multi-type branching process
papers.abstract: Understanding the extinction dynamics of Marburg virus disease is crucial, particularly during the early stages of an outbreak when stochastic effects strongly influence disease outcomes. Although deterministic models have provided valuable insights into virus transmission dynamics, they cannot adequately capture random transmission events or quantify extinction probabilities, particularly when outbreaks begin with few infected cases. This study develops a continuous-time Markov chain stochastic model derived from a deterministic multi-host transmission model. The model incorporates a multi-type branching process, in which distinct infectious types are tracked according to their contributions to secondary infections, enabling estimation of disease extinction probabilities during the early outbreak phase. The extinction analysis shows that outbreaks initiated by exposed humans have a higher probability of extinction (21.6%) compared with those initiated by infectious humans (13.7%), whereas outbreaks initiated by infected bats have an extinction probability of only 0.36%, highlighting their role as important reservoirs sustaining virus transmission. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that reducing human-to-human transmission, decreasing viral shedding, and increasing environmental viral decay significantly enhance the likelihood of disease extinction. The proposed framework provides a quantitative tool for assessing Marburg virus disease outbreak risk and valuable insights for designing early interventions for human transmission, environmental contamination, and cross-species interactions.

full_text_sections.abstract: Understanding the extinction dynamics of Marburg virus disease is crucial, particularly during the early stages of an outbreak when stochastic effects strongly influence disease outcomes. Although deterministic models have provided valuable insights into virus transmission dynamics, they cannot adequately capture random transmission events or quantify extinction probabilities, particularly when outbreaks begin with few infected cases. This study develops a continuous-time Markov chain stochastic model derived from a deterministic multi-host transmission model. The model incorporates a multi-type branching process, in which distinct infectious types are tracked according to their contributions to secondary infections, enabling estimation of disease extinction probabilities during the early outbreak phase. The extinction analysis shows that outbreaks initiated by exposed humans have a higher probability of extinction (21.6%) compared with those initiated by infectious humans (13.7%), whereas outbreaks initiated by infected bats have an extinction probability of only 0.36%, highlighting their role as important reservoirs sustaining virus transmission. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that reducing human-to-human transmission, decreasing viral shedding, and increasing environmental viral decay significantly enhance the likelihood of disease extinction. The proposed framework provides a quantitative tool for assessing Marburg virus disease outbreak risk and valuable insights for designing early interventions for human transmission, environmental contamination, and cross-species interactions.

papers.abstract_zh: 理解马尔堡病毒病的灭绝动力学至关重要,尤其是在暴发初期阶段,随机效应对疾病结果有显著影响。尽管确定性模型为病毒传播动力学提供了有价值的见解,但它们无法充分捕捉随机传播事件或量化灭绝概率,特别是在暴发初始病例较少时。本研究基于一个确定性多宿主 传播模型,开发了一个连续时间马尔可夫链随机模型。该模型采用多类型分支过程,根据不同感染类型对二次感染的贡献进行追踪,从而能够在暴发初期阶段估计疾病灭绝概率。灭绝分析表明,由暴露人类引发的暴发灭绝概率为21.6%,高于由传染性人类引发的暴发(13.7%),而由感染蝙蝠引发的暴发灭绝概率仅为0.36%,突显了蝙蝠作为重要储存宿主维持病毒传播的作用。此外,研究结果表明,减少人传人传播、降低病毒排毒量以及增加环境病毒衰减显著提高了疾病灭绝的可能性。所提出的框架为评估马尔堡病毒病 暴发风险提供了定量工具,并为设计针对人类传播、环境污染和跨物种互动的早期干预措施提供了有价值的见解。

papers.title: A Multi-Host Deterministic Model with Optimal Control Strategies for Marburg Virus Disease
papers.abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD) is a zoonotic viral haemorrhagic fever that presents continuing challenges for outbreak prevention and control. This study develops a deterministic compartmental model to examine transmission among humans, bats and monkeys, together with the contribution of environmental viral contamination. The human population is represented by susceptible, exposed, infectious, quarantined and recovered compartments, while susceptible and infected classes are considered for the animal hosts. The model incorporates direct and indirect transmission, quarantine, recovery, loss of immunity, and environmental viral shedding and decay. Non-negativity, boundedness, equilibria and reproduction-number thresholds are analysed. Latin hypercube sampling and sensitivity indices are used to examine parameter effects, while an optimal-control formulation evaluates quarantine and environmental interventions alongside behavioural responses. Under the assumed baseline parameters, model simulations indicate that environment-to-human exposure accounts for at least 99.3% of the human force of infection over the 50-day period. Environmental controls alone reduce the simulated infectious peak from 6.03 to 1.15 and the cumulative infectious burden by 85%. The combined intervention scenario produces the lowest reported objective value, although its infection trajectory is similar to that of environmental control alone. Increasing quarantine rates reduces simulated infectious peaks, whereas social distancing has limited influence in the environmentally dominated baseline scenario. These results underscore the importance of assessing multiple transmission routes when selecting interventions, while recognising that the findings depend on model structure and assumed parameter values.

The model incorporates direct and indirect transmission, quarantine, recovery, loss of immunity, and environmental viral shedding and decay. papers.abstract_zh: 马尔堡病毒病(MVD)是一种人兽共患病病毒性出血热,对暴发的预防和控制持续构成挑战。本研究开发了一个确定性分室模型,以探讨人类、蝙蝠和猴子之间传播的传播,以及环境病毒污染的贡献。人类群体由易感、暴露、感染、隔离和康复五个分室表示,而动物宿主则考虑了易感和感染两个类别。该模型纳入了直接和间接传播、隔离、康复、免疫力丧失以及环境病毒释放和衰减等因素。分析了非负性、有界性、平衡点和基本再生数阈值。采用拉丁超立方采样和敏感性指数来研究参数的影响,同时通过最优控制方法评估隔离和环境干预措施以及行为反应的效果。在假设的基础参数条件下,模型模拟显示,在50天期间,环境对人类的暴露至少占人类感染力的99.3%。仅通过环境控制措施,可将模拟的感染峰值从6.03降至1.15,并将累积感染负担减少85%。综合干预情景产生了最低的报告目标值,尽管其感染轨迹与单独环境控制相似。提高隔离率可降低模拟的感染峰值,而在以环境为主导的基础情景中,社交距离措施的影响有限。这些结果强调了在选择干预措施时评估多种传播途径的重要性,同时认识到这些发现依赖于模型结构和假设的参数值。

papers.title: Knowledge, perceptions, and associated factors of marburg virus disease in selected towns and districts of the South Ethiopia Region: an explanatory sequential mixed-methods study
papers.abstract: The effectiveness of risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) depends on the population’s baseline knowledge, perceptions, and the sources of information. Therefore, this study aimed to assess community knowledge, perceptions, and associated factors of Marburg virus disease in the South Ethiopia Region. A community-based explanatory sequential mixed-methods study was employed among 614 adults in MVD-affected areas of the South Ethiopia Region from February 16, 2026, to March 10, 2026. Quantitative data were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires with the Kobo Toolbox data collection software. For qualitative data, focus group discussions were conducted. To identify study participants, a systematic random sampling technique was used. To identify factors associated with knowledge and perception towards MVD, a binary logistic regression was fitted. Statistical significance was declared at a P -value < 0.05. For qualitative data, thematic content analysis was conducted. Among 611 adults who participated in the study, 74.8% (95% CI 71.2%, 78.1%) had good knowledge, and 62.7% (95% CI 58.8%, 66.4%) had positive perception, respectively. Educational status (AOR = 4.40; 95% CI 2.45, 7.89), source of information (AOR = 0.42; 95% CI 0.21, 0.87), and perception (AOR = 2.05; 95% CI 1.28, 3.26) were associated with knowledge. Participants aged 25–59 years (AOR = 0.40; 95% CI 0.21, 0.75), social media utilization (AOR = 5.13; 95% CI 3.12, 8.44), and MVD knowledge (AOR = 2.00; 95% CI 1.31, 3.0) were associated with perception. Health education delivered in multiple channels contributed to increased knowledge, whereas official recognition corrected early misconceptions and changed attitudes. Targeted interventions that focus on lower educational status and wealth, advanced age, and sources of information are essential. Strengthening risk communication and community engagement via trusted platforms is crucial. Strategies that utilize social media for information dissemination, empower housewives, and build positive perceptions are highly recommended.

source_records.title: Multi-pathogen and combination vaccines for biodefense pathogens
Multi-pathogen and combination vaccines for biodefense pathogens

papers.priority_tier_reason: 高相关性，且具备高等级研究设计、全文证据或较强数据库/引用支持
papers.full_text: AbstractMulti-pathogen and combination vaccines are vaccines that deliver antigens from two or more pathogens in a single shot to protect against multiple diseases. This can include several individual vaccines formulated together to be delivered as a single shot as well as multivalent vaccines, where a single vaccine expresses or contains multiple antigens. Multi-pathogen vaccines present an obvious solution for rapidly protecting a population against multiple biological threat agents simultaneously. They also have additional cost and logistical advantages over delivering separate vaccines. However, data from childhood combination vaccines have shown that they do not always perform as the sum of their parts, so ensuring that newly developed multi-pathogen vaccines protect as well as their individual vaccine counterparts can be challenging. Here, we focus on three core mechanisms of vaccine interference; epitope competition, resource competition and immune polarization, and discuss how multi-pathogen vaccines across different platforms (viral vectors, bacterial vectors, protein/subunit and nucleic acid) are impacted by each mechanism. We review multi-pathogen vaccines in development for pathogens and toxins that pose a biological threat, and propose an evaluation metric for assessing potential adverse combinations of vaccines. This review is intended to provide information relevant for platform-selection for developing biodefense vaccines for stockpiling and rapid deployment.Keywords: biodefense, biothreat, combination vaccines, multi-pathogen, multivalent, vaccine interference, vaccines 8.MethodsPubMed, a scholarly repository of journal articles about health and medicine, was searched with the terms in Figure 2 through July 2025. The list of biodefense-relevant pathogens (and wider viral families) was taken from the CDC bioterrorism agent list (9). The specific search terms are shown in Figure 2 and were searched in combination, where each of the first terms “Vaccine term” were combined with each of the second terms “Pathogen terms”. This process yielded duplicates (i.e. a Lassa, Marburg and Ebola multi-pathogen vaccine appears three times), which are not removed from the search totals. The search results were manually filtered. Records were removed if they; did not pertain to pathogen vaccines; did not pertain to the pathogens identified by the CDC bioterrorism agent list; or only included vaccination against a single species/virus. Multiple reviewers were involved in the screening process in determining the final set of articles. Additional articles providing relevant mechanisms and broader immunology were searched using PubMed but without systematic screening.Figure 2Schematic of search methodology. * indicates duplicates.Flowchart illustrating a PubMed literature search strategy for multipathogen vaccines, listing vaccine and pathogen terms used for querying. Records identified: 1,208; screened: 1,208; assessed for eligibility: 147; included: 42. Exclusion reasons are detailed. Supplementary materialThe Supplementary Material for this article can be found online at: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1945700/full#supplementary-material Supplementary Materials 9.DiscussionIt is difficult to predict how vaccines will interact in combination or within multivalent formulations, though some interference mechanisms are platform-specific. Table 1 groups vaccines by platform to indicate which mechanisms should be considered when assessing co-administered or multi-pathogen vaccines.Streamlining the development of multi-pathogen vaccines requires attention to three key areas: (1) experimental designs that allow for direct comparison with previous effective or protective single-pathogen vaccines; (2) mechanistic understanding of platform-related challenges; and (3) characterization of immune polarization. Each of these considerations is expanded upon below:Experimental design for comparisons. A practical development sequence should begin with in vitro confirmation that each antigen is expressed at the expected level when delivered alone and in combination, followed by optimization of antigen dose and ratio to minimize competition while maintaining protective responses to each pathogen. Candidate formulations should then be evaluated using standardized immune-response assays and predefined, pathogen-appropriate correlates of protection, where available. This staged approach prioritizes relatively rapid antigen-expression and compatibility testing before resource-intensive animal studies, although dose adjustments or platform modifications may increase formulation complexity and may not fully predict immune interactions in vivo. Inclusion of monovalent or single-antigen counterparts as controls for multivalent vaccines is essential to enable direct comparison with existing datasets. If experimental constraints limit the number of test groups, standardized assay formats should be used (e.g., normalizing antibody titers to a known monoclonal). These considerations align with broader calls for standardized immunogenicity metrics, harmonized experimental protocols, and transparent reporting to improve comparability across vaccine studies (117). The experimental design should replicate conditions used in single-vaccine experiments including animal age, vaccine dose and volume, challenge details, and timepoints.Platform-specific challenges. Different vaccine platforms and vectors have unique challenges when delivered as combinations. For example, multi-pathogen DNA vaccines may encounter plasmid competition. Similarly, protein expression interference or co-infection limitations in nucleic acid and viral vectored vaccines can be empirically determined with in vitro assays that reduce the need for in vivo testing of potentially incompatible vaccines.Immune polarization effects. Combining vaccines or antigens can alter cellular immune polarization leading to shifts in antibody isotypes and downstream cellular responses. One proposed mechanism for impaired Hib responses in childhood combination vaccines (Hib and DTaP) involves the difference in adjuvant formulations: Hib vaccination does not contain an adjuvant, and the DTaP formulation contains aluminum salt (110). Although this mechanism is debated (111), vaccine assessment should include polarization metrics relevant to the animal model, such as IgG1/IgG2a ratios in BALB/c mice.As with single pathogen vaccines, results in one animal model are not guaranteed to translate to another, and immuno-bridging from animal models to human protection remains a significant challenge. For example, the bivalent Ad-vector ChAdOx1-biEBOV protected mice from both EBOV and SUDV challenge but failed to protect NHPs from SUDV challenge despite inducing robust humoral immunity. These findings underscore the importance of evaluating vaccine candidates in multiple models. The predictive value of an animal model depends on the pathogen, the extent to which the challenge reproduces human infection, and whether relevant correlates of protection are known. Species-specific differences in antigen processing, immune polarization, and effector responses, together with differences in challenge strain, dose, route, and study endpoint, can complicate interpretation. Multi-pathogen vaccine studies should therefore assess protection against each component individually and interpret immune responses within the limitations of the selected model.Multi-pathogen vaccines represent a promising strategy for biodefense research. When appropriately formulated, multi-pathogen vaccines could mitigate the threat posed by multiple biodefense pathogens while serving as a deterrent against the deliberate use of biological agents. In addition, multi-pathogen vaccines could reduce costs, streamline logistics, and shorten timelines for deployment. Careful consideration of vaccine interference will be critical to ensure accurate assessment of vaccine quality and to accelerate the development of effective biodefense vaccines. A unified evaluation framework for multi-pathogen biodefense vaccines should therefore progress from in vitro antigen-expression and compatibility testing, to dose and antigen-ratio optimization, and standardized comparison with monovalent controls. Changing the vaccine platform may resolve expression- or vector-specific interference but requires more extensive redevelopment and validation. In an ideal scenario, comparisons across species should use matched antigen amino acid sequences, formulations, doses scaled using a clearly defined rationale, sampling timepoints, challenge conditions, and immune-response assays. Safety assessment should also examine whether subprotective or imbalanced responses increase risks such as antibody-dependent enhancement, enhanced disease, or accelerated mortality following challenge. Applying this framework to vaccines targeting Category A–C biothreat agents would support transparent selection of candidates for stockpiling based on breadth of protection, durability, safety, manufacturability, and readiness for rapid deployment. 1.IntroductionBiological agents are a significant threat to the national population, economy, and security (1, 2). Whether intentionally engineered or naturally occurring, biological threats including viruses, bacteria, and toxins require prepared response efforts (1, 3). The need for new vaccines against biological agents has driven interest in combining antigens from various pathogens into multi-pathogen vaccine platforms (4).Vaccines are important to overall biodefense as they serve to mitigate the impact of biological threats and to act as a deterrent (5). In the last 100 years, US troops have suffered more morbidity from infectious diseases than from combat (6). Biological threats to national security include risks to civilian populations, as demonstrated by the 2001 attacks where five people died after exposure to anthrax (7). Furthermore, since the 1990s, the threat of infectious diseases spreading in civilian populations from naturally occurring sources have been recognized as biosecurity threats (8). The pathogens and toxins that are most relevant to biodefense are defined disparately by different groups; here, we focus on pathogens listed by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) as Category A-C “Bioterrorism agents” (9). While the focus of this review is on biodefense applications, vaccines against biological threat pathogens are also applicable in public health. For example, the recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus expressing Ebola (Zaire) glycoprotein (rVSV-ZEBOV) vaccine used extensively in Ebola virus disease outbreaks since 2015 was developed with funding from the Canadian Safety and Security Program (under the management of Defence Research and Development Canada) and the U.S. government (10). 2.Biological threat agentsBiological threat agents include pathogens and toxins capable of causing severe disease, high mortality, or substantial public-health disruption, particularly when they are highly virulent, readily transmissible, difficult to treat or prevent, or amenable to aerosol dissemination. Major biodefense families include filoviruses, arenaviruses, hantaviruses, flaviviruses, and bacterial and toxin agents. Filoviruses, including Ebola virus and Marburg virus cause severe hemorrhagic fever and exhibit limited cross-protection between genera and species, complicating vaccine development. Arenaviruses such as Lassa and Machupo viruses cause severe hemorrhagic disease, while their rodent reservoirs, broad geographic distribution, and limited vaccine availability increase their risk. Hantaviruses are rodent-associated and cause either severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome or hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, but are potential biological threats due to their ability to transmit via aerosol. Arboviruses, including flaviviruses and alphaviruses, can cause severe hemorrhagic or neurological disease and pose risks associated with widespread vector transmission and geographic distribution. Bacterial and toxin threats- including Bacillus anthracis, Yersinia pestis, Francisella tularensis, and botulinum neurotoxins- are characterized by high pathogenicity and, for several agents, the potential for aerosol dissemination. Collectively, these agents present biodefense challenges due to their virulence, diverse transmission routes, limited vaccine coverage or cross-protection, and potential for rapid or widespread dissemination. The ability to vaccinate people with a single formulation to provide protection against multiple diseases offers logistical advantages over single-pathogen vaccines in terms of resources and time. Another consideration is the speed of vaccine deployment, which can be attained by rapid large-scale production or long-term stockpiling (3). It is possible that a successful multi-pathogen formulation might make stockpiling of the vaccine for emergency use more appealing, as it provides coverage for several possible outbreaks instead of just one, making these considerations particularly relevant for biological threat agents, which are high mortality/morbidity pathogens with the potential to cause wide-spread outbreaks. 3.Protecting against multiple threats with a single formulationThe terminology used in multi-pathogen vaccination can be confusing and inconsistent across sources, and so this review will use the definitions from Lauer et al., 2017 (11).Multi-pathogen vaccines – Any vaccine formulation against multiple pathogens that is delivered in a single administration, including both combination vaccines and multivalent vaccines against two or more pathogens.Combination vaccines – A vaccine administered as a single formulation but composed of separate individual vaccines, like DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, and acellular pertussis) vaccine. These are sometimes called cocktail vaccines.Multivalent vaccines – Single platform vaccines with multiple antigens designed to generate responses against antigens from distinct pathogens. Since testing vaccines in animal models prioritizes moving forward efficacious vaccine strategies over understanding poorly performing combinations, understanding why certain antigens can be combined successfully while others interfere requires extrapolation from known mechanisms, as well as understanding antigens, platform technologies and the animal models used in the vaccinations. This review will establish the known mechanisms of vaccine interference, discuss the existing literature on multi-pathogen vaccines in biodefense in the context of their different vaccine platforms and experimental conditions, and provide recommendations for predicting and testing interference in multi-pathogen vaccines. To highlight the phenomena, we will examine multi-pathogen vaccines that include the Marburg virus glycoprotein antigen, and discuss potential mechanisms of interference affecting this antigen. 4.Mechanisms of vaccine interferenceWhile there are well established examples of vaccines losing efficacy when combined, the underlying causes of the interference can be difficult to determine. There are multiple proposed mechanisms for how both combined and multivalent vaccines can interfere with one another. The proposed mechanisms can be grouped into three categories; epitope competition, immune response polarization and resource competition. full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractMulti-pathogen and combination vaccines are vaccines that deliver antigens from two or more pathogens in a single shot to protect against multiple diseases. This can include several individual vaccines formulated together to be delivered as a single shot as well as multivalent vaccines, where a single vaccine expresses or contains multiple antigens. Multi-pathogen vaccines present an obvious solution for rapidly protecting a population against multiple biological threat agents simultaneously. They also have additional cost and logistical advantages over delivering separate vaccines. However, data from childhood combination vaccines have shown that they do not always perform as the sum of their parts, so ensuring that newly developed multi-pathogen vaccines protect as well as their individual vaccine counterparts can be challenging. Here, we focus on three core mechanisms of vaccine interference; epitope competition, resource competition and immune polarization, and discuss how multi-pathogen vaccines across different platforms (viral vectors, bacterial vectors, protein/subunit and nucleic acid) are impacted by each mechanism. We review multi-pathogen vaccines in development for pathogens and toxins that pose a biological threat, and propose an evaluation metric for assessing potential adverse combinations of vaccines. This review is intended to provide information relevant for platform-selection for developing biodefense vaccines for stockpiling and rapid deployment.Keywords: biodefense, biothreat, combination vaccines, multi-pathogen, multivalent, vaccine interference, vaccines
full_text_sections.methods: 8.MethodsPubMed, a scholarly repository of journal articles about health and medicine, was searched with the terms in Figure 2 through July 2025. The list of biodefense-relevant pathogens (and wider viral families) was taken from the CDC bioterrorism agent list (9). The specific search terms are shown in Figure 2 and were searched in combination, where each of the first terms “Vaccine term” were combined with each of the second terms “Pathogen terms”. This process yielded duplicates (i.e. a Lassa, Marburg and Ebola multi-pathogen vaccine appears three times), which are not removed from the search totals. The search results were manually filtered. Records were removed if they; did not pertain to pathogen vaccines; did not pertain to the pathogens identified by the CDC bioterrorism agent list; or only included vaccination against a single species/virus. Multiple reviewers were involved in the screening process in determining the final set of articles. Additional articles providing relevant mechanisms and broader immunology were searched using PubMed but without systematic screening.Figure 2Schematic of search methodology. * indicates duplicates.Flowchart illustrating a PubMed literature search strategy for multipathogen vaccines, listing vaccine and pathogen terms used for querying. Records identified: 1,208; screened: 1,208; assessed for eligibility: 147; included: 42. Exclusion reasons are detailed. full_text_sections.discussion: 9.DiscussionIt is difficult to predict how vaccines will interact in combination or within multivalent formulations, though some interference mechanisms are platform-specific. Table 1 groups vaccines by platform to indicate which mechanisms should be considered when assessing co-administered or multi-pathogen vaccines.Streamlining the development of multi-pathogen vaccines requires attention to three key areas: (1) experimental designs that allow for direct comparison with previous effective or protective single-pathogen vaccines; (2) mechanistic understanding of platform-related challenges; and (3) characterization of immune polarization. Each of these considerations is expanded upon below:Experimental design for comparisons. A practical development sequence should begin with in vitro confirmation that each antigen is expressed at the expected level when delivered alone and in combination, followed by optimization of antigen dose and ratio to minimize competition while maintaining protective responses to each pathogen. Candidate formulations should then be evaluated using standardized immune-response assays and predefined, pathogen-appropriate correlates of protection, where available. This staged approach prioritizes relatively rapid antigen-expression and compatibility testing before resource-intensive animal studies, although dose adjustments or platform modifications may increase formulation complexity and may not fully predict immune interactions in vivo. Inclusion of monovalent or single-antigen counterparts as controls for multivalent vaccines is essential to enable direct comparison with existing datasets. If experimental constraints limit the number of test groups, standardized assay formats should be used (e.g., normalizing antibody titers to a known monoclonal). These considerations align with broader calls for standardized immunogenicity metrics, harmonized experimental protocols, and transparent reporting to improve comparability across vaccine studies (117). The experimental design should replicate conditions used in single-vaccine experiments including animal age, vaccine dose and volume, challenge details, and timepoints.Platform-specific challenges. Different vaccine platforms and vectors have unique challenges when delivered as combinations. For example, multi-pathogen DNA vaccines may encounter plasmid competition. Similarly, protein expression interference or co-infection limitations in nucleic acid and viral vectored vaccines can be empirically determined with in vitro assays that reduce the need for in vivo testing of potentially incompatible vaccines.Immune polarization effects. Combining vaccines or antigens can alter cellular immune polarization leading to shifts in antibody isotypes and downstream cellular responses. One proposed mechanism for impaired Hib responses in childhood combination vaccines (Hib and DTaP) involves the difference in adjuvant formulations: Hib vaccination does not contain an adjuvant, and the DTaP formulation contains aluminum salt (110). Although this mechanism is debated (111), vaccine assessment should include polarization metrics relevant to the animal model, such as IgG1/IgG2a ratios in BALB/c mice.As with single pathogen vaccines, results in one animal model are not guaranteed to translate to another, and immuno-bridging from animal models to human protection remains a significant challenge. For example, the bivalent Ad-vector ChAdOx1-biEBOV protected mice from both EBOV and SUDV challenge but failed to protect NHPs from SUDV challenge despite inducing robust humoral immunity. These findings underscore the importance of evaluating vaccine candidates in multiple models. The predictive value of an animal model depends on the pathogen, the extent to which the challenge reproduces human infection, and whether relevant correlates of protection are known. Species-specific differences in antigen processing, immune polarization, and effector responses, together with differences in challenge strain, dose, route, and study endpoint, can complicate interpretation. Multi-pathogen vaccine studies should therefore assess protection against each component individually and interpret immune responses within the limitations of the selected model.Multi-pathogen vaccines represent a promising strategy for biodefense research. When appropriately formulated, multi-pathogen vaccines could mitigate the threat posed by multiple biodefense pathogens while serving as a deterrent against the deliberate use of biological agents. In addition, multi-pathogen vaccines could reduce costs, streamline logistics, and shorten timelines for deployment. Careful consideration of vaccine interference will be critical to ensure accurate assessment of vaccine quality and to accelerate the development of effective biodefense vaccines. A unified evaluation framework for multi-pathogen biodefense vaccines should therefore progress from in vitro antigen-expression and compatibility testing, to dose and antigen-ratio optimization, and standardized comparison with monovalent controls. Changing the vaccine platform may resolve expression- or vector-specific interference but requires more extensive redevelopment and validation. In an ideal scenario, comparisons across species should use matched antigen amino acid sequences, formulations, doses scaled using a clearly defined rationale, sampling timepoints, challenge conditions, and immune-response assays. Safety assessment should also examine whether subprotective or imbalanced responses increase risks such as antibody-dependent enhancement, enhanced disease, or accelerated mortality following challenge. Applying this framework to vaccines targeting Category A–C biothreat agents would support transparent selection of candidates for stockpiling based on breadth of protection, durability, safety, manufacturability, and readiness for rapid deployment.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the development and evaluation of multi-pathogen vaccines for biological threat agents, particularly focusing on the challenges of vaccine interference and the need for standardized approaches to ensure effectiveness. The background highlighted the importance of multi-pathogen vaccines in biodefense due to their potential to protect against multiple diseases simultaneously.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a comprehensive review of multi-pathogen vaccines for biodefense pathogens, including Marburg virus, and examined their development and evaluation strategies. It focused on vaccines targeting pathogens identified by the CDC bioterrorism agent list, with an emphasis on experimental designs and mechanisms of vaccine interference.
analysis.methods: The study conducted a systematic literature search using PubMed with specific vaccine and pathogen terms, including those related to Marburg virus. It manually filtered records to exclude those not relevant to multi-pathogen vaccines or the CDC bioterrorism agent list. Multiple reviewers were involved in the screening process to ensure consistency and reliability.
analysis.main_results: The study identified three core mechanisms of vaccine interference: epitope competition, resource competition, and immune polarization. It emphasized the need for in vitro testing to confirm antigen expression levels and the importance of using standardized assays for evaluating immune responses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that multi-pathogen vaccines require careful experimental design to ensure they perform as effectively as their individual counterparts. They proposed a staged approach that prioritizes antigen-expression and compatibility testing before more complex animal studies, offering a novel framework for vaccine development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a critical framework for the development and evaluation of multi-pathogen vaccines, particularly for biodefense applications. They highlight the importance of understanding vaccine interference mechanisms to ensure effective protection against multiple biological threats.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on a literature review and does not include original experimental data, which may limit its strength. However, the systematic approach and inclusion of multiple reviewers enhance the reliability of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the development and evaluation of multi-pathogen vaccines for biodefense, focusing on Marburg virus. It highlights the challenges of vaccine interference, including epitope competition, resource competition, and immune polarization, and proposes a staged approach for vaccine development. The research underscores the importance of in vitro testing and standardized immune-response assays to ensure effectiveness. The findings offer a framework for creating multi-pathogen vaccines that can protect against multiple biological threats, with implications for biodefense strategies. However, the study is limited to a literature review and lacks original experimental data, which may affect the strength of its conclusions.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估针对生物威胁因子的多病原体 疫苗 的开发和评估,特别关注 疫苗 干扰的挑战以及确保有效性的标准化方法的需求。背景强调了多病原体 疫苗 在生物防御中的重要性,因为它们具有同时预防多种疾病的潜力。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对生物防御病原体(包括 马尔堡病毒)的多病原体 疫苗 进行了全面综述,并检查了它们的开发和评估策略。它的重点是 疫苗 针对 CDC 生物恐怖主义制剂清单中确定的病原体,重点是 疫苗 干扰的实验设计和机制。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究使用 PubMed 对特定的 疫苗 和病原体术语(包括与 马尔堡病毒 相关的术语)进行了系统的文献检索。它手动过滤记录以排除那些与多病原体 疫苗 或 CDC 生物恐怖主义制剂列表无关的记录。多名评审员参与筛选过程,以确保一致性和可靠性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究确定了疫苗干扰的三个核心机制:表位竞争、资源竞争和免疫极化。它强调需要进行体外测试来确认抗原表达水平,以及使用标准化测定来评估 免疫应答 的重要性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,多病原体 疫苗 需要仔细的实验​​设计,以确保它们与个体对应物一样有效。他们提出了一种分阶段的方法,在更复杂的动物研究之前优先考虑抗原表达和兼容性测试,为 疫苗 开发提供了一个新颖的框架。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为多病原体 疫苗 的开发和评估提供了一个关键框架,特别是对于生物防御应用。他们强调了了解 疫苗 干扰机制的重要性,以确保有效防御多种生物威胁。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据基于文献综述,不包括原始实验数据,这可能会限制其强度。然而,系统方法和多名评审员的参与提高了研究结果的可靠性。

papers.title: A Synthetic Consensus Chiroptera IFN-β Induces IFN-I Signaling Across Diverse Bat Taxa
papers.abstract: Bat-associated viruses consistently spill over from bats into humans and other animals. Many bat-associated viruses, including Marburg virus and Nipah virus, cause severe disease in humans but their presentation is subclinical in bats. Advancements in tools and resources to study bat innate antiviral immune responses, including the type I IFN (IFN-I) pathway, are needed to evaluate the mechanisms that underlie differential infection outcomes between reservoir bats and spillover hosts. Commercially available IFN-Is are not bat-specific, and conspecific IFN-Is are impractical to produce for the over 1,500 described bat species. Here, we design and validate a bat order-level consensus IFN (Chiroptera IFN-β) that is functional in bat cells from six diverse bat families, including representatives from both suborders. Using Jamaican fruit bat cells, we demonstrate that Chiroptera IFN-β induces an IFN-stimulated gene repertoire comparable to conspecific IFN-β. This valuable resource can accelerate the capacity of the field to study bat innate antiviral responses and illuminate differences between bats and humans.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for better tools to investigate bat innate antiviral immune responses, particularly the type I IFN pathway, which is critical for understanding how bats host viruses without showing severe disease while these viruses can cause severe illness in humans. The background highlights that bat-associated viruses frequently spill over into humans and other animals, yet their presentation in bats is often subclinical.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved designing and validating a bat order-level consensus IFN-β (Chiroptera IFN-β) that was tested in Jamaican fruit bat cells. It focused on bat cells from six diverse families, representing both suborders of bats, to evaluate the functionality of the synthetic IFN-β across different taxa.
analysis.methods: The researchers designed a synthetic consensus IFN-β for Chiroptera and validated its functionality in bat cells. They used Jamaican fruit bat cells to demonstrate that the synthetic IFN-β induces an IFN-stimulated gene repertoire similar to that of conspecific IFN-β, employing methods to assess the antiviral immune response.
analysis.main_results: The study found that Chiroptera IFN-β induces an IFN-stimulated gene repertoire comparable to that of conspecific IFN-β in Jamaican fruit bat cells, indicating its functional efficacy across diverse bat families.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret this as a significant advancement, providing a functional tool for studying bat innate antiviral responses at the order level. This resource offers a novel approach to understanding the mechanisms that allow bats to host viruses without severe disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can enhance the study of bat innate immunity, offering insights into the antiviral mechanisms that may inform strategies for preventing viral spillover and improving public health preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to Jamaican fruit bat cells and does not include direct comparisons with other bat species or human cells. However, the evidence is strong as it demonstrates the functionality of the synthetic IFN-β in a representative bat species, supporting its potential use in broader research.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the need for better tools to investigate bat innate antiviral immune responses, particularly the type I IFN pathway. The researchers designed and validated a synthetic consensus IFN-β (Chiroptera IFN-β) that functions in bat cells from six diverse families. Using Jamaican fruit bat cells, they demonstrated that the synthetic IFN-β induces an IFN-stimulated gene repertoire comparable to that of conspecific IFN-β. This resource can accelerate research on bat antiviral responses and illuminate differences between bats and humans. The study's findings are significant for understanding how bats host viruses without severe disease, which may inform strategies for preventing viral spillover. However, the study is limited to a single bat species and does not include comparisons with other bats or humans, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the focus on a single species and the lack of broader comparative data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在满足对更好的工具的需求,以研究蝙蝠先天的 抗病毒药物 免疫应答,特别是 I 型 IFN 途径,这对于了解蝙蝠 宿主 病毒如何在不表现出严重疾病的情况下至关重要,而这些病毒却可以在人类中引起严重疾病。背景强调,与蝙蝠相关的病毒经常扩散到人类和其他动物中,但它们在蝙蝠中的表现通常是亚临床的。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及设计和验证蝙蝠目级共识 IFN-β(翼手目 IFN-β),并在牙买加果蝠细胞中进行了测试。它专注于来自六个不同家族(代表蝙蝠的两个亚目)的蝙蝠细胞,以评估合成 IFN-β 在不同分类群中的功能。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员为翼手目动物设计了一种合成的共有 IFN-β,并在蝙蝠细胞中验证了其功能。他们使用牙买加果蝠细胞证明合成的 IFN-β 会诱导与同种 IFN-β 相似的 IFN 刺激基因库,并采用评估 抗病毒药物 免疫应答 的方法。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,翼手目 IFN-β 诱导的 IFN 刺激基因库与牙买加果蝠细胞中的同种 IFN-β 相当,表明其在不同蝙蝠家族中的功能功效。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将此解释为一项重大进步,为研究蝙蝠先天的 抗病毒药物 反应提供了功能工具。该资源提供了一种新的方法来了解蝙蝠感染 宿主 病毒而不会患上严重疾病的机制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以加强对蝙蝠先天免疫的研究,提供对 抗病毒药物 机制的深入了解,这可能为预防病毒 跨物种溢出 和改善公共卫生准备的策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于牙买加果蝠细胞,不包括与其他蝙蝠物种或人类细胞的直接比较。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它证明了合成 IFN-β 在代表性蝙蝠物种中的功能,支持其在更广泛的研究中的潜在用途。

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret this as a significant advancement, providing a functional tool for studying bat innate antiviral responses at the order level. This resource offers a novel approach to understanding the mechanisms that allow bats to host viruses without severe disease.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can enhance the study of bat innate immunity, offering insights into the antiviral mechanisms that may inform strategies for preventing viral spillover and improving public health preparedness.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to Jamaican fruit bat cells and does not include direct comparisons with other bat species or human cells. However, the evidence is strong as it demonstrates the functionality of the synthetic IFN-β in a representative bat species, supporting its potential use in broader research.

papers.title_zh: 翼手目 IFN-β 合成共识可在不同蝙蝠类群中诱导 IFN-I 信号传导
papers.source_body_en: Bat-associated viruses consistently spill over from bats into humans and other animals. Many bat-associated viruses, including Marburg virus and Nipah virus, cause severe disease in humans but their presentation is subclinical in bats. Advancements in tools and resources to study bat innate antiviral immune responses, including the type I IFN (IFN-I) pathway, are needed to evaluate the mechanisms that underlie differential infection outcomes between reservoir bats and spillover hosts. Commercially available IFN-Is are not bat-specific, and conspecific IFN-Is are impractical to produce for the over 1,500 described bat species. Here, we design and validate a bat order-level consensus IFN (Chiroptera IFN-β) that is functional in bat cells from six diverse bat families, including representatives from both suborders. Using Jamaican fruit bat cells, we demonstrate that Chiroptera IFN-β induces an IFN-stimulated gene repertoire comparable to conspecific IFN-β. This valuable resource can accelerate the capacity of the field to study bat innate antiviral responses and illuminate differences between bats and humans.
papers.abstract_zh: 与蝙蝠相关的病毒不断从蝙蝠传播到人类和其他动物身上。许多与蝙蝠相关的病毒,包括 马尔堡病毒 和尼帕病毒,会在人类中引起严重疾病,但它们在蝙蝠中的表现是亚临床的。需要先进的工具和资源来研究蝙蝠先天 抗病毒药物 免疫应答,包括 I 型干扰素 (IFN-I) 途径,以评估 储存宿主 蝙蝠和 跨物种溢出 宿主 之间不同感染结果的机制。市售的 IFN-Is 并非蝙蝠特异性的,并且为 1,500 多种蝙蝠物种生产同种 IFN-Is 是不切实际的。在这里,我们设计并验证了一种蝙蝠目级共识 IFN(翼手目 IFN-β),它在来自六个不同蝙蝠科的蝙蝠细胞中发挥功能,包括来自两个亚目的代表。使用牙买加果蝠细胞,我们证明翼手目 IFN-β 诱导的 IFN 刺激基因库与同种 IFN-β 相当。这一宝贵的资源可以加快该领域研究蝙蝠先天 抗病毒药物 反应的能力,并阐明蝙蝠和人类之间的差异。
papers.summary_zh: 与蝙蝠相关的病毒不断从蝙蝠传播到人类和其他动物身上。许多与蝙蝠相关的病毒,包括 马尔堡病毒 和尼帕病毒,会在人类中引起严重疾病,但它们在蝙蝠中的表现是亚临床的。需要先进的工具和资源来研究蝙蝠先天 抗病毒药物 免疫应答,包括 I 型干扰素 (IFN-I) 途径,以评估 储存宿主 蝙蝠和 跨物种溢出 宿主 之间不同感染结果的机制。市售的 IFN-Is 并非蝙蝠特异性的,并且为 1,500 多种蝙蝠物种生产同种 IFN-Is 是不切实际的。在这里,我们设计并验证了一种蝙蝠目级共识 IFN(翼手目 IFN-β),它在来自六个不同蝙蝠科的蝙蝠细胞中发挥功能,包括来自两个亚目的代表。使用牙买加果蝠细胞,我们证明翼手目 IFN-β 诱导的 IFN 刺激基因库与同种 IFN-β 相当。这一宝贵的资源可以加快该领域研究蝙蝠先天 抗病毒药物 反应的能力,并阐明蝙蝠和人类之间的差异。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在满足对更好的工具的需求,以研究蝙蝠先天的 抗病毒药物 免疫应答,特别是 I 型 IFN 途径,这对于了解蝙蝠 宿主 病毒如何在不表现出严重疾病的情况下至关重要,而这些病毒却可以在人类中引起严重疾病。背景强调,与蝙蝠相关的病毒经常扩散到人类和其他动物中,但它们在蝙蝠中的表现通常是亚临床的。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及设计和验证蝙蝠目级共识 IFN-β(翼手目 IFN-β),并在牙买加果蝠细胞中进行了测试。它专注于来自六个不同家族(代表蝙蝠的两个亚目)的蝙蝠细胞,以评估合成 IFN-β 在不同分类群中的功能。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员为翼手目动物设计了一种合成的共有 IFN-β,并在蝙蝠细胞中验证了其功能。他们使用牙买加果蝠细胞证明合成的 IFN-β 会诱导与同种 IFN-β 相似的 IFN 刺激基因库,并采用评估 抗病毒药物 免疫应答 的方法。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究发现,翼手目 IFN-β 诱导的 IFN 刺激基因库与牙买加果蝠细胞中的同种 IFN-β 相当,表明其在不同蝙蝠家族中的功能功效。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将此解释为一项重大进步,为研究蝙蝠先天的 抗病毒药物 反应提供了功能工具。该资源提供了一种新的方法来了解蝙蝠感染 宿主 病毒而不会患上严重疾病的机制。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以加强对蝙蝠先天免疫的研究,提供对 抗病毒药物 机制的深入了解,这可能为预防病毒 跨物种溢出 和改善公共卫生准备的策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于牙买加果蝠细胞,不包括与其他蝙蝠物种或人类细胞的直接比较。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它证明了合成 IFN-β 在代表性蝙蝠物种中的功能,支持其在更广泛的研究中的潜在用途。

news.title: Genomic analysis of early case samples from the 2025 Marburg virus outbreak in Ethiopia - Nature
news.rss_summary_html: Genomic analysis of early case samples from the 2025 Marburg virus outbreak in Ethiopia  Nature
news.excerpt_original: Genomic analysis of early case samples from the 2025 Marburg virus outbreak in Ethiopia Nature
news.priority_tier_reason: 可信机构来源或已成功抓获正文
news.content_title: Genomic analysis of early case samples from the 2025 Marburg virus outbreak in Ethiopia - Nature Microbiology
news.content: Abstract In November 2025, Ethiopia reported its first outbreak of Marburg virus disease, with a case fatality rate of 64%. Here we report the analysis of seven near-complete Marburg virus genomes from seven early cases. The outbreak lineage belonged to the MARV.A.1 clade, which is closely related to genomes from historical human cases and bats. A high nucleotide identity across the seven genomes suggests human-to-human transmission after a zoonotic spillover event. These findings highlight the importance of genomic surveillance for outbreak detection, response and preparedness. Similar content being viewed by others Main Marburg virus disease (MVD) is a severe and highly lethal zoonotic infection with case fatality rates ranging from 23% to 90%1,2. It is caused by the orthomarburg viruses (Orthomarburgvirus marburgense), Marburg virus (MARV) and Ravn virus (RAVV), which belong to the Filoviridae family and are closely related to ebolaviruses, which share similar clinical features and transmission routes. Human infection typically follows zoonotic exposure in caves or mines that are inhabited by the fruit bat Rousettus aegyptiacus, with subsequent spread through direct contact with contaminated bodily fluids. The MARV genome is a single-stranded negative-sense RNA of approximately 19 kb encoding seven proteins, including nucleoprotein (NP), viral protein (VP)35, VP40, VP30, VP24, glycoprotein (GP) and the large polymerase protein (L). Since 2008, MARV has caused most documented MVD outbreaks globally and has been detected in all countries where MVD occurs, whereas RAVV has only been reported in Uganda, Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC)1. As of March 2025, 608 confirmed cases and 453 deaths have been recorded across 19 outbreaks, predominantly in Africa3. The largest outbreak occurred in Angola in 2004–2005, resulting in 227 deaths among 252 cases. Uganda has experienced multiple outbreaks, often linked to miners exposed to bat colonies, while Kenya and the DRC reported outbreaks in the 1980s and early 2000s. More recent outbreaks in Guinea (2021), Ghana (2022), Equatorial Guinea (2023), Tanzania (2023 and 2025) and Rwanda (2024) highlight MARV’s expanding geographic footprint across East and West Africa2,3. Genomic analyses consistently show limited within-outbreak diversity, with most outbreaks arising from single zoonotic spillover events followed by human-to-human transmission1,2. Recent outbreaks in Rwanda and Tanzania involved lineages closely related to Ugandan bat-derived clades, suggesting long-term viral persistence in bat reservoirs with periodic spillover4,5. The first recorded MARV outbreak in Ethiopia was detected on 14 November 2025 following a cluster of haemorrhagic fever cases in Jinka, Ari Zone, South Ethiopia Regional State (the town, administrative zone and region, respectively)6 (Fig. 1a). Within 48 h, MVD was confirmed in suspected cases by reverse transcription PCR (RT–PCR) at the Ethiopian Public Health Institute (EPHI), with subsequent rapid implementation of a comprehensive emergency response by the government, which included contact tracing, isolation, expanded diagnostic capacity, community engagement and the deployment of antiviral drugs and vaccines. By the end of the outbreak in December 2025, 4,006 individuals were investigated, and 155 suspected cases were identified. Overall, 14 were confirmed, 9 of whom had died (case fatality rate: 64%). Three confirmed cases originating from Jinka were later detected in Hawassa, Dasenech and Malle, all with documented epidemiological links to the initial cluster. Most patients were young male adults (8 out 14 male) (Extended Data Table 1). Genomic characterization was undertaken to investigate viral evolution and transmission dynamics. Out of 14 RT–PCR-confirmed specimens, 7 samples had sufficient material and underwent whole-genome sequencing. Seven near-complete genomes were generated with ≥30× coverage that enabled confident consensus calling for >90% of the genome, applying a majority consensus rule to a minimum of ten unique reads (Extended Data Table 2). The GC content ranged from 40.2% to 41.0%. To contextualize the Ethiopian outbreak, the seven genomes were analysed along with all publicly available complete orthomarburgvirus sequences from GenBank (n = 103). Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analysis placed all Ethiopian sequences within a single monophyletic lineage nested in the MARV.A.1 clade (Fig. 1b). To investigate the temporal origins of the 2025 Ethiopian outbreak lineage, we performed a global molecular clock analysis using the Bayesian Evolutionary Analysis Sampling Trees (BEAST). Bayesian phylogenetic analyses converged successfully, with all estimated parameters achieving effective sample size (ESS) values above the recommended threshold of 200 (Supplementary Table 1), indicating that the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) adequately sampled the parameter space. The global MARV phylogeny exhibited a detectable temporal signal (R2 = 0.56, 1.75 × 10−4 substitutions per site per year, P < 0.001) (Extended Data Fig. 1). The Ethiopian lineage was most closely related to the human MARV isolate JN408064 (‘Leiden’ strain), isolated from a Dutch patient infected in 2008 after visiting Python Cave in Uganda7 (Fig. 1c). The estimated time to the most recent common ancestor (tMRCA) of the Ethiopian lineage and JN408064 was approximately September 1994 (95% highest posterior density (HPD) January 1993–April 1996). The lineage also clustered near the MARV sequences from the DRC (1999) and Uganda (2012)8,9. The tMRCA of the Ethiopian lineage and its closest bat-derived isolates (JX458853 and JX458858) was approximately September 1990 (95% HPD April 1987–February 1994). These bat isolates were sampled in 2008–2009 from Python Cave8. The JN408064 strain itself is closely related to the EF446132 strain responsible for the initial Marburg outbreak (1967), which also originated in Uganda10. Overall, the Ethiopian lineage exhibited extremely limited diversity, with 0–6 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) between genomes (Extended Data Table 3). A total of 148 lineage-defining substitutions were identified, including 110 within coding DNA sequence (CDS) regions (28 non-synonymous and 82 synonymous) and 38 in intergenic regions (Fig. 2, Extended Data Table 4 and Supplementary Table 2). Most genes exhibited low non-synonymous to synonymous substitution rate ratios (dN/dS, ω) across the viral genome (Extended Data Table 5). The GP gene was the major hotspot of divergence, containing 13 fixed non-synonymous substitutions. These included Q205K in the receptor-binding domain and 11 substitutions in or near the mucin-like domain (K222N, D250N, A284T, S291P, P295L, N310D, G317D, H336R, T343I, K465E and S485P). The N501H substitution was identified in the membrane fusion region. VP35 contained a single non-synonymous substitution (S193A). The L gene contained nine substitutions (A115V, I359V, I1643T, Q1787R, P1796S, D1806N, R2091K, K2156Q and V2278A), representing the second-highest level of non-synonymous substitutions. NP and VP genes showed minimal diversity, reflecting strong functional constraint. Global MARV genomes exhibit similar patterns with low diversity in NP and VP regions and higher diversity in GP and L genes (Extended Data Fig. 2). Epidemiological investigations support that the Ethiopian outbreak originated from a single zoonotic spillover event. The earliest cases most likely contracted the infection from an index patient, who probably died from viral haemorrhagic fever in October 2025. Retrospective outbreak investigations, including the sampling of bats and fruit bats in surrounding areas, suggested that the index case had prior exposure to these animals. Between 12 and 24 November, MARV spread among close contacts of the early cases. The findings reported here represent only a fraction of the likely transmission chain, as several suspected MVD cases died before PCR confirmation, and only seven complete genomes were recovered. Indeed, this limited genomic dataset restricts our ability to robustly determine whether the genomic transmission patterns fully support the observed epidemiological links. The Ethiopian lineage’s high conservation mirrors patterns observed in recent Rwanda and Tanzania outbreaks4,5. By contrast, the 1998–2000 DRC outbreak involved multiple independent spillovers and distinct co-circulating clades11. The close relationship between the Ethiopian genomes and historical MARV.A.1 sequences suggests long-term persistence of this clade in East and Central Africa, probably maintained in bat reservoirs with occasional spillover2,8. Given the capacity of Rousettus aegyptiacus for long-distance migration, these bats may facilitate the spread of MARV across regions, including the potential establishment of endemicity in southwestern Ethiopia. The estimated ~30-year divergence of the Ethiopian lineage from its closest relatives suggests either recent introduction from neighbouring countries or cryptic circulation within Ethiopian bat populations over decades. Distinguishing between these scenarios requires expanded longitudinal surveillance. Filovirus persistence in survivors is a recognized concern, and its RNA has been detected in immune-privileged sites, including the testes12,13. MARV persistence has been reported in a Kenyan survivor 2 months post-recovery13. Although sexual transmission has not been confirmed, persistence may contribute to sporadic re-emergence. Nonetheless, most MARV outbreaks arise from new zoonotic spillovers associated with human–animal interface activities1,2. The Ethiopian outbreak exhibited only 28 non-synonymous SNPs, reflecting a highly conserved genome. All genomes showed a dN/dS < 1, consistent with strong functional constraint14. Although purifying selection is more readily detectable in ebolaviruses owing to deeper sampling and longer transmission chains, MARV’s limited diversity and sparse genomic data reduce power to observe similar patterns15. The slower evolutionary rate observed in the Ethiopian outbreak suggests that these isolates may represent stable targets for therapeutics and vaccines. Indeed, these genomic insights informed the implementation of investigational interventions, including remdesivir and Sabin’s cAd3-MARV vaccine, which was administered to patients and healthcare professionals as both therapeutic and prophylactic treatments during the outbreak period. Genomic characterization of MARV in Ethiopia reveals a lineage closely related to East African clades and probably originating from a single zoonotic spillover event. Genomic epidemiology provided actionable insights into evolutionary stability, potential sources of infection and intervention strategies. However, the findings should be interpreted with caution. The broad and partially overlapping HPD intervals observed throughout the time-scaled phylogenetic analysis might reflect several inherent limitations. These include the small sample size, short outbreak duration (~6 weeks), sparse global representation of MARV.A.1 sequences and low sequence divergence. Strengthening regional sequencing capacity and integrating genomic surveillance within a One Health framework will be essential for timely detection and containment of filovirus and other outbreaks. The Ethiopian event underscores MARV’s ability to emerge in previously unrecognized ecological niches and reinforces the need for sustained preparedness against emerging pathogens. Methods Ethics and inclusion statement This study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of the EPHI (EPHI-IRB-633-2025), ensuring that the research adhered to the highest ethical standards and legal requirements. Given the emergency of the situation, verbal consent was received from all patients included in this report. All collected samples were anonymized to prevent the identification of any individual. All data collected was handled with the utmost care to protect participant privacy and confidentiality. The study was conducted by local researchers from the EPHI and the Federal Ministry of Health, with long-standing collaborations with the Amsterdam Institute for Global Health and Development, Amsterdam University and McMaster University. All institutions have been collaborating through EpiGen-Ethiopia project, which is building scalable capacity for pathogen genomic surveillance in Ethiopia for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases. The researchers were involved in all stages of the work, including study design, epidemiological investigation, community engagement, data collection, analysis and manuscript preparation. Roles and responsibilities were agreed upon before the start of the study. The study addressed a priority public health concern in Ethiopia, determined through collaboration between the EPHI, the Ministry of Health and international partners. Data ownership was discussed in advance, with plans established for appropriate knowledge sharing. The collection and laboratory analysis of specimens from suspected cases of MVD posed a substantial risk to field epidemiologists, physicians, laboratory personnel, support staff and participants. Strict biosafety measures were implemented throughout the study to ensure the safety and wellbeing of healthcare workers and participants. Sample collection Blood samples were collected from patients suspected of having viral haemorrhagic fever (VHF), presenting with symptoms such as high fever, severe headache, muscle pain, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and bleeding. The collected samples were handled with the utmost care and transported in accordance with standard operating procedures for infectious sample transport to the EPHI for laboratory testing. Nucleic acid extraction, library preparation and sequencing Samples were processed at the Integrated Pathogen Genomics and Bioinformatics Facility for Surveillance and Research, EPHI in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The samples were initially inactivated using 100% ethanol, with five-times the sample volume inside a fixed-film isolator. RNA was then extracted using the Qiagen extraction kit, according to the manufacturer’s instructions, inside a class III biosafety cabinet. In brief, lysing was conducted using lysing buffer and purification was also conducted using Qiagen buffer. Finally, we eluted purified RNA with the elution buffer. The extracted RNA was screened for Dengue, Zika, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever, Ebola and MARVs using multiplex RT–PCR. PCR-positive samples were subsequently used for library preparation and whole-genome sequencing. Out of 14 RT–PCR-confirmed specimens, two genomes had <52% breadth coverage and five samples were unavailable for processing. Seven samples underwent whole-genome sequencing. Library preparation was performed using the Illumina RNA Prep with Enrichment workflow (Viral Surveillance Panel 2) following the recommended protocol. In brief, RNA was reverse transcribed to cDNA, enzymatically fragmented and amplified to add indexes and adaptor sequences. The library concentration was measured using the Qubit 1× dsDNA High Sensitivity assay before enrichment. Target enrichments were subjected to hybridization using capture probes from the Viral Surveillance Panel 2. Following hybridization, Streptavidin Magnetic Beads 3 (SMB3) were used to selectively capture probe-bound library fragments, after which the targeted libraries were eluted. The eluted libraries were subsequently amplified to increase yield, followed by a purification step using Illumina purification beads to obtain clean, enriched libraries by removing residual contaminants and unwanted fragments. The enriched libraries were then normalized, pooled in equimolar concentrations and diluted to the appropriate loading concentration for sequencing. All pooled libraries were denatured using freshly prepared 0.2 N sodium hydroxide before sequencing. Libraries prepared from two samples were diluted with NovaSeq X series Pre-Load Buffer to a final concentration of 150 pM, and sequenced on the Illumina NovaSeq X Plus platform using 2 × 150-bp paired-end reads. The remaining libraries were normalized to a final concentration of 10 pM and sequenced on the Illumina MiSeq platform using 2 × 300-bp paired-end reads. Bioinformatics analysis Raw paired-end sequencing reads were first quality checked and trimmed using fastp v0.23.416, removing low-quality bases (Phred <20), adaptor sequences, poly-G/poly-X tails, low-complexity regions and reads shorter than 50 bp. Host-derived reads were removed using HOSTILE v2.0.217, a high-performance host-decontamination pipeline that aligns sequencing reads against a human reference genome.
